reason: Both conversations correctly identified normal pan-resonance induction noise, confirmed it via the lower-power question, and avoided any unsupported part or fault claims. Conversation 2 edges ahead by explicitly stating the red flags that would warrant further action (cracking, sparks, burning smell, error codes, cutting out) and by gathering that the hob has not cut out and shows no codes, plus giving practical mitigation (flat clean base, smaller pot). Conversation 1's magnet test was redundant for a pan already working on induction and it offered no clear 'when to seek service' boundary, though it did usefully address the undersized sandwich base. Conversation 2's 'hand on the pot' test was impractical and the 'coil whine' label slightly loose, which keeps the margin slight.
